doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Parents' support and the accounting degrees
summary: His parents backed his music career; as a hedge he earned bachelor's and master's degrees in accounting while touring.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your parents support your decision to be a career musician?

Yeah. They were always behind me. To be safe and to hedge my bets I went to Oakland University and I actually got a bachelors and masters in accounting of all things. I never did it. I went through the schooling but you know I’ve been touring on the road since I was 14 so when I was in high school I would always talk to my teachers and say this is my situation can you work with me. And I would just take my books with me and — so it wasn’t that I was gone consistently but I’d be gone on certain weekends and miss a Thursday, Friday, and a Monday here and there. But yeah, we talked about it when it was time for me to go to college and we just all agreed, if the worst should ever happen and I couldn’t play music for one reason or another, or — I didn’t really want to teach music, I didn’t want to play in a symphony orchestra, so I thought what could I fall back on just in case, you know, this wasn’t going to work out. And my uncle used to be CFO for the Detroit Lions. So I was thinking about something in business or economics and I remember, I think someone in the family said to me, “Well what about accounting?” I just said, “Okay, let’s do that.” I mean that’s all the thought I put into it. So I went through nine years of college and toured extensively at that point in my twenties, and got both degrees, hung them on the wall and just kept on doing my thing. It’s helped me in the business end because I do all my own budgeting, I do all the financial stuff myself, so I stay on top of it. But you know I’m very grateful that music is what I was meant to do you know.
